subject: Trial bump vs credits — GreenLeaf bridge request
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Craig Thompson <ctw@greenleafhealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick: trial bump vs credits for the last two weeks

Hi Craig —

Thanks for the update on internal testing. I dug into the usage and the week‑3 report attached shows a spike (mostly embedding calls from the patient-matching flow). We want to keep GreenLeaf moving without breaking procurement cadence. Two practical options for the short term:

1) Two‑week trial bump (same GA terms, no additional charge) — extends your sandbox access through Dec 7 so your team finishes the integration tests.
2) One‑time usage credit ($8k) that covers the overage and keeps the trial end date unchanged. Credits would be applied to the first invoice if you move to a committed plan.

Pros/cons: bump is lower friction for engineering but needs an express legal nod (MOA addendum). Credit is faster for procurement but pushes the engineering timeline tighter.

Can you confirm which you prefer? If you need us to draft a short addendum I can loop Ben and Kim.

Attachments: greenleaf-week3-usage.csv (usage breakdown)

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
From: Craig Thompson <ctw@greenleafhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick: trial bump vs credits for the last two weeks

Naomi —

Appreciate the breakdown. Engineering would prefer the two‑week bump so they can finish verification without the sprint getting cramped. Procurement: we need a letter or short addendum to sign; our legal team is sensitive to open-ended extensions.

If you can send a one‑page addendum that just extends the sandbox window (no change to commercial terms) and confirms no data retention changes, I can route it for approval.

CCing procurement@greenleafhealth.com to make sure they see this.

—Craig
CTO, GreenLeaf Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Quick: trial bump vs credits for the last two weeks

Ben / Kim —

GreenLeaf wants the two‑week bump and procurement wants an addendum. Can we ship a minimal legal addendum (1 page) that:
- extends the evaluation period by 14 days (new expiry Dec 7, 2026)
- states there is no change to fees or data handling
- confirms Redwood will apply no automatic conversion during the extension

Ben: pricing/credits perspective — is it OK to offer bump without a discount or should we attach a small engagement credit as goodwill?
Kim: can you confirm the wording and whether procurement will accept a short MOA addendum or require a PO/CLIN?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15m if helpful.

Naomi
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick: trial bump vs credits for the last two weeks

Short answer: bump-only is fine but I recommend adding a $2,500 trial credit on conversion (applied to first invoice) — it keeps procurement happy without setting a precedent for future free extensions. Suggest language: "Redwood agrees to extend the Evaluation Period by 14 days. Should Customer convert to a paid Redwood plan within 30 days of the Evaluation Period, Redwood will issue a one-time credit of $2,500 to the Customer's first invoice."

Operational note: flag to finance — credits over $5k need manager signoff; $2.5k is low friction.

I can draft the line and Naomi can include it in the addendum.

—Ben
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks for confirming. Naomi — attaching the one‑page addendum as requested (GreenLeaf_MOA_draft.pdf). High level:
- Evaluation extended to 11 Dec 2026 (we agreed Dec 7 above but procurement asked for EOW; changed to 11 Dec for alignment with their review cycle).
- No change to fees or data retention.
